profile_text.body:
Arm designs and provides compute platforms for artificial intelligence across cloud, edge, and embedded systems, serving what it describes as innovators worldwide. Founded in 1990 and headquartered in Cambridge, United Kingdom, the public company positions itself at the intersection of AI and compute convergence, offering performance, efficiency, and flexibility for applications ranging from data centers to autonomous machines. The company describes its platform as connecting cloud, edge, and physical AI with consistent software and a scalable ecosystem.

The company's AI offerings include the Arm AI Portal, which developers and agents can use to discover optimized models, evaluate performance, and access deployment workflows. Arm has also launched the AGI CPU and describes enabling agentic AI that reshapes data center operations through scalable orchestration across cloud and edge environments. The company emphasizes edge AI for consumer and embedded devices, positioning its compute as real-time, private, and power-efficient, and markets solutions for autonomous vehicles and robotics through what it calls AI-defined compute. It also highlights NVIDIA DGX Spark, built on Arm-based NVIDIA Grace Blackwell technology, as a tool for developing and running large AI models.

The held facts record eight MCP servers associated with Arm's registry presence, spanning data observability, calendar integration, contractor search, career frameworks, pharmaceutical data lookup, advertising bidding, pharma vendor services, and a fishing game.
